title.narrative: Secondary Education Sector Investment Program - Tranche 1

description.narrative: The proposed investment program will support the government's reform of secondary education (grades 6-12) into a system that builds the foundation for a skilled labor force and prepares youths to meet the requirements of a rapidly developing economy. It will support advanced teaching and learning programs that use information and communication technology (ICT), as well as prevocational and vocational programs, teacher development, and examination reforms. It will promote gender-equitable and pro-poor stipends for students. It will help establish more decentralized and efficient allocation and use of resources, as well as strengthen sector performance monitoring. The investment program will build upon the ongoing Secondary Education Sector Development Program and the Second Teaching Quality Improvement Project. It will further benefit from the experience of the Third Primary Education Development Project, which uses disbursement-linked indicators (DLIs). The investment program links disbursement to the achievement of key results. It will further support the transition to a sector-wide approach.

title.narrative: Loan 3047: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 25 Nov 2024

Progress Toward Outcome: Different policy documents as National Curriculum Policy Framework (NCPF), Institutional Development Plan (IDP), Comprehensive Review of Secondary Education Stipend Program, HSP Operational Manual, Pre-vocational and Vocational Implementation Plan (PVIP), Annual Sector Performance Report (ASPR), etc. developed and approved. Science equipment and Teaching learning materials supplied. Establishment of 100 low-cost schools, extension of 46 DEOs, construction of TSEOs (4), establishment of 710 ILC completed. Different categories of training as PST, LSB, PBM, CQ, HT management training provided to significant number of teachers.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Feb 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44213/44213-016-apfs-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Jul 2021: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/44213/44213-016-44213-017-smr-en.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: - SHED, MoE approved the National Curriculum Policy Framework (NCPF) on 14 Nov 2017. The NCPF has been designed to make the curriculum socially inclusive and responsive to the skill required by the society. The Curriculum Implementation Plan (CIP) has also been revised in 2017 in alignment with the NCPF. Review of curriculum completed in September 2019 and preparation of new curriculum in progress following the guidelines of NCPF. - A Curriculum Implementation Plan (CIP) was developed and approved in 2014 to ensure implementation of curriculum in the classroom. The Plan was subsequently revised in 2017. The CIP included the provision for training of teachers in five core subjects for effective delivery of curriculum in the classroom. Training of the teachers for effective delivery of curriculum in the classroom through use of teacher's curriculum guides (TCGs) commenced in June 2017. The program completed in December 2019 through training of 200539 teachers (F 47425) including 42274 (F 9309) madrasah teachers. - Practical science teaching in the schools has been completed through supply of equipment to the selected schools and training of teachers. All the secondary level science teachers (both school and madrasah) [total 63,609 {School 52,581 (F: 6439) and Madrasah: 13273 (F: 1797)}] trained on practical oriented science teaching. Equipment supplies to the selected schools and madrasahs completed for 10000 institutions [School: 7163 (Girls: 766); Madrasah; 2837 (Girls: 531)]. These activities were completed in Dec 2019. - Science equipment was distributed to four zones (Mymensingh, Cumilla, Rajshahi, Khulna) under Tranche 1 (Package No. GD-5). In the selected zones total number of girls schools are 1516 and equipment was distributed to 766 girls' schools based on the selection criteria to include the underprivileged and remote schools. - The ICT Learning Centers (ILCs) were selected based on electricity and network connectivity as well as to maintain regional parity. For this, a total of 104 girls' school were included in the list instead of targeted number 128. - Secondary Teacher Development Strategy (STDS) approved by the SHED on 31 December 2019. - Training on Continuous Assessment (SBA renamed as CA) commenced in October 2019 and a total of 25053 (F 6210) teachers completed. 46616 teachers have already been trained by June 2022. - A report drafted containing MOE's policy guideline on minimum standard of school building construction to improve learning environment and gender-responsiveness through wider stakeholder consultation. The report was presented at SHED on 05 April and 05 July last subsequently wherein a few policy directives obtained to recast the report. Modification of the report in progress targeting completion by September 2021. - Selection of 100 institutions (schools and madrasah) completed and works completed in 100 sites. - Independent review of existing stipend program was completed and a Harmonized Stipend Program (HSP) was developed through a study. SHED, MoE has approved the HSP on 16 January 2019. The program has been adopted as a key scheme under SEDP (SESIP Tranche 3). All the stipend programs were integrated within the harmonized scheme from January 2020. HSP targets equally to all genders, including third gender, and thus is socially inclusive Eligible boys and girls at secondary level from grades 6-12 including Madrasahs, judged in accordance with approved criteria are within the purview of stipend irrespective of geographical locations. 100% students from small ethnic community, third gender, special needs, previous enclave areas, especially derived children, and successors of freedom fighters will be eligible for stipend. An HSP manual has also been prepared under SESIP and approved by SHED. - The Prime Minister's Education Assistance Trust office has been implementing the harmonized stipend program since July 2020. A review of the HSP can be done after implementation of the program for at least 2-3 years. Therefore, a third-party evaluation on the impact of HSP is not feasible during SESIP period. - Management of MPO (salary of nongovernment teachers) decentralized from DSHE to all nine Zonal Education Offices from June 2015. - A policy guideline has been developed to strengthen the capacity of EMIS. supported by an international EMIS consultant, submitted to DSHE in April 2019. The report is now being reviewed by DSHE for approval and implementation of recommendations. - Annual Secondary Education Performance Report with improved indicators and sex-disaggregated data prepared and published in November 2017. The ASPR was also prepared for 2018. The final draft report for 2019 has been prepared and under review by DSHE for finalization. A meeting on PPT presentation of ASPR 2019 took place on 29 June 2022 and decision came out that a workshop would be organized with all stakeholders for its broader presentation and analysis. - A Secondary Education Sector Program Framework (SE-SPF) was developed in 2017 under SESIP through two consecutive Joint Sector Reviews involving all the secondary sector stakeholders and key development partners which acted as the baseline document for SEDP. - AFR for FY 2013-14, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19 and 2019-20 completed. Based on the AFR, the PFM Action Plan is being updated annually with identified actions for development of procurement and financial practices and implementation monitored quarterly. -
